questions.question: The scientific study of the relationship of living things and their environment is known by which term?
questions.explanation: Ecology is the scientific study of the relationship of living things and their environment.

questions.question: The word ecology emanated from which Greek term?
questions.explanation: The word ecology emanated from the Greek word Oikos meaning house or home.

questions.question: The biosphere is seen as a gigantic household consisting of all which units?
questions.explanation: The biosphere is seen as a gigantic household otherwise known as ecosystems.

questions.question: An ecosystem is an integrated unit consisting of interacting plants and which other organism group?
questions.explanation: An ecosystem consists of interacting plants and animals whose survival depends on abiotic and biotic structures.

questions.question: The basic and most important concept of an ecosystem is that everything is related to which of the following?
questions.explanation: The basic concept is that everything is related to everything else.

questions.question: Environmental factors that affect the life and development of an organism are regarded as which factor type?
questions.explanation: Physical factors are all external conditions and influences affecting the life and development of an organism.

questions.question: If any environmental factor is less than ideal, it will become which factor in plant growth?
questions.explanation: If any environmental factor is less than ideal it will become a limiting factor in plant growth.

questions.question: Most plant problems are caused by which stress type?
questions.explanation: Most plant problems are caused by environmental stress, either directly or indirectly.

questions.question: On average, approximately what percentage of solar energy is used in primary productivity?
questions.explanation: On average approximately only 2-3 per cent of solar energy is used in primary productivity.

questions.question: The intensity or concentration of sunlight is referred to by which term?
questions.explanation: Light quantity refers to the intensity or concentration of sunlight.

questions.question: Light quality refers to the color or which property reaching the plant surface?
questions.explanation: Light quality refers to the color or wavelength reaching the plant surface.

questions.question: Which light colors have the greatest effect on plant growth?
questions.explanation: Red and blue light have the greatest effect on plant growth.

questions.question: Which light color is least effective for plants as most plants reflect it?
questions.explanation: Green light is least effective to plants as most plants reflect green light.

questions.question: Blue light is primarily responsible for which plant process?
questions.explanation: Blue light is primarily responsible for vegetative growth.

questions.question: Red light when combined with blue light encourages which process in plants?
questions.explanation: Red light when combined with blue light encourages flowering in plants.

questions.question: Fluorescent or cool-white light is high in which range of light quality?
questions.explanation: Fluorescent or cool-white light is high in the blue range of light quality.

questions.question: Incandescent light is high in which range of light quality?
questions.explanation: Incandescent light is high in the red or orange range.

questions.question: The intensity of light at which plants no longer carry on photosynthesis or when photosynthesis balances respiration is known by which term?
questions.explanation: The intensity of light at which plants no longer carry on photosynthesis or when photosynthesis balances respiration is called compensation intensity.

questions.question: The temperature at which physiological processes are at their maximum efficiency is known by which term?
questions.explanation: The temperature at which physiological processes are at their maximum efficiency is called optimum temperature.

questions.question: The minimum, optimum and maximum temperatures are known by which term?
questions.explanation: The minimum, optimum and maximum temperatures are called cardinal temperatures.

questions.question: In extremely low temperature, the protoplasm may be frozen into which state?
questions.explanation: In extremely low temperature, the protoplasm may be frozen to ice.

questions.question: In extremely high temperature, the protein may undergo which change?
questions.explanation: In extremely high temperature, the protein may coagulate.

questions.question: The rate of transpiration increases with an increase in which factor?
questions.explanation: The rate of transpiration increases with increase in atmospheric temperature.

questions.question: The misuse of water leads to soil degradation and which other process?
questions.explanation: The misuse of water leads to soil degradation and erosion.

questions.question: All physiological processes take place in which medium?
questions.explanation: All the physiological processes take place in the medium of water.

questions.question: Plants living in water require large quantities of water and are known by which term?
questions.explanation: Hydrophytes are plants living in water that require large quantities of water.

questions.question: Terrestrial plants which cannot tolerate extremely dry conditions are known by which term?
questions.explanation: Xerophytes are terrestrial plants which cannot tolerate extremely dry conditions.

questions.question: Terrestrial plants that require moderate quantities of water are known by which term?
questions.explanation: Mesophytes are terrestrial plants requiring moderate quantity of water.

questions.question: The main source of soil water is which source?
questions.explanation: The main source of soil water is precipitation.

questions.question: The interchange of water between earth's surface and the atmosphere is known as which cycle?
questions.explanation: Rainfall occurs due to interchange of water between earth's surface and the atmosphere, known as the hydrologic cycle.

questions.question: Evergreen forests in tropical regions are found due to which condition?
questions.explanation: Evergreen forests in tropical regions are found due to heavy rainfall throughout the year.

questions.question: The quantity of water that a soil holds or that infiltrates into the soil depends upon the properties of soil and which other factor?
questions.explanation: The quantity of water depends upon the properties of soil and type and density of vegetation covering it.

questions.question: Atmospheric moisture in the form of invisible vapour is known by which term?
questions.explanation: Atmospheric moisture in the form of invisible vapour is known as humidity.

questions.question: Low temperature causes higher relative humidity by decreasing the capacity of air for which substance?
questions.explanation: Low temperature causes higher relative humidity by decreasing the capacity of air for moisture.

questions.question: Air in motion is known by which term?
questions.explanation: Air in motion is called wind.

questions.question: Wind accelerates transpiration, removes solid moisture and at high velocities causes which effect?
questions.explanation: Wind at high velocities causes soil erosion.

questions.question: Excessive transpiration leads to desiccation and death of which plant part?
questions.explanation: Excessive transpiration leads to desiccation and death of apical meristems.

questions.question: Plants on exposed mountain tops frequently are in danger of being uprooted and blown away by which force?
questions.explanation: Plants on exposed mountain tops are frequently in danger of being uprooted and blown away by strong winds.

questions.question: Vegetation on exposed mountain tops is largely composed of species with which growth type?
questions.explanation: In these situations, vegetation is largely composed of species with a prostrate habit of growth.

questions.question: The factors concerned with the physical geography of the earth are known by which term?
questions.explanation: The factors concerned with physical geography of the earth are known as topographic factors.

questions.question: As altitude above sea level increases, there happens a decrease in temperature and which other factor?
questions.explanation: As altitude increases, there happens a decrease of temperature and pressure.

questions.question: In the northern hemisphere, which slope receives more solar radiation than the north facing slope?
questions.explanation: In the northern hemisphere, south facing slopes receives more solar radiation than the north facing slope.

questions.question: The steepness of a slope accelerates the downward movement of which substance?
questions.explanation: The steepness of slope accelerates the downward movement of surface water.

questions.question: The direction of mountain chains considerably influences which factor in an area?
questions.explanation: The direction of mountain chains considerably influences the rainfall in an area.

questions.question: If mountain chains lie in the path of wind full of water vapour, then there is heavy rainfall on which side?
questions.explanation: If mountain chains lie in the path of wind full of water vapour, then there is heavy rainfall on the wind striking side.

questions.question: Edaphic factors deal with different aspects of which component?
questions.explanation: Edaphic factors deal with different aspects of soil.

questions.question: Soil is usually defined as any part of earth's crust supporting which growth?
questions.explanation: Soil is defined as any part of earth's crust in which plants root.

questions.question: Soil is constituted as a result of long-term process of complex interaction leading to the production of which matrix type?
questions.explanation: Soil is constituted as a result of complex interaction leading to the production of a mineral matrix.

questions.question: Which of the following is a main component of soil?
questions.explanation: Soil mainly has mineral matter as a component.

questions.question: All life on the earth is maintained by the flow of energy radiated by which source?
questions.explanation: All life on the earth is maintained by the flow of energy radiated by the sun.
